n: A new song for new wonders: God’s ‘right hand’ and ‘holy arm’ — his own power — have won the victory without human help.
God has made his salvation known openly, for all the nations to see.
God remembered his covenant love and faithfulness to Israel, and the ends of the earth saw him save. Mary’s song in Luke echoes this verse.

f.w: all the ends of the earth

n: All the earth is invited to break out in joyful shouts and songs. This verse inspired the hymn ‘Joy to the World.’
The harp and the singing voice combine in praise.

f.g: A lyre, the stringed instrument David played.

n: Trumpets and the ram’s horn blast out as at a king’s coronation. The Lord is hailed as King.
The sea and everything living on the earth join the celebration.
Rivers clap their hands and mountains sing for joy — beautiful poetic images of all creation celebrating.

f.w: Let the floods clap their hands

n: Creation rejoices because the Lord is coming to judge the world with perfect fairness. Latter-day revelation ties this to the Second Coming.

f.w: for he cometh to judge the earth
